fieldNotes.truckGate: Single primary entrance road off GA Highway 247 in the NW. The entrance road crosses the BNSF/Norfolk Southern mainline at a grade crossing (confirmed in Street View) then runs into the secured plant property. The whole campus is fenced; the controlled entrance is a clear pinch-point.
fieldNotes.guardShack: A guard booth is almost certainly present at this flagship secured plant - the largest Frito-Lay snack plant in the US with 1000+ employees and tightly controlled internal roads. However it could not be directly confirmed: Street View does not reach the internal entrance road and z20-z21 satellite at the gate zone is washed out. Marked true at medium confidence.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: Truck staging/parking lot with parked trailers in the SW of the property (confirmed at z20), providing pre-/post-gate holding room.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large internal paved aprons and a roundabout-style distribution junction between the gate and the dock banks - ample inside holding room.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long entrance road from GA-247 plus expansive internal road network and staging lots - holds well over 3 trucks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide entrance road and large paved aprons with significant unused width - room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Single primary entrance road off GA-247 serves both in and out.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Estimated 1 inbound; satellite resolution limits exact count - low confidence.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Long dock banks on multiple building faces (east face of the main plant and the NW warehouse face) with many trailers backed in. Total estimated ~70 - 50+ band.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Massive trailer drop yard on the east side with hundreds of trailers in long rows, plus the SW staging lot - far exceeds 50 stalls.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock banks on physically distinct building faces (east face and NW warehouse) indicating separate shipping/receiving clusters.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town location in Kathleen/Houston County GA, surrounded by farmland and open fields; small-town industrial setting - Rural.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus character: the main plant mass plus a separate NW warehouse building and process/utility structures - multiple large building clusters on one property.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale clearly identifiable - low confidence, possible but not confirmed.
fieldNotes.railServed: Confirmed - a rail mainline runs along the west; rail spurs penetrate the plant property and rail tank cars are parked on-site (visible in z19 imagery on the SW side).
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter box yields ~130 acres for the very large plant campus, consistent with the largest US Frito-Lay snack plant.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~320 trailers counted across the east drop yard, dock faces, and SW staging - approximate.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: Overhead count estimate; dock faces partially obscured by trailers and washed-out imagery - moderate confidence.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Possible second checkpoint given the internal road system and rail crossing, but not confirmed - left false.
